name: Dark Contrast Banner
description: A full-width band with a deep surface, soft gradient orbs behind the content, and a single primary action. It reads as a deliberate “pause” between lighter sections and adds depth without clutter.

source_reference.when_to_use: After a long light section or before a footer; when you want one clear next step (book, start trial, view pricing) with high contrast.
source_reference.do_not: Stack multiple competing buttons or long paragraphs—this pattern works because it stays sparse and confident.
source_reference.description: A full-width band with a deep surface, soft gradient orbs behind the content, and a single primary action. It reads as a deliberate “pause” between lighter sections and adds depth without clutter.

name: Split Screen CTA
description: A two-column layout with copy and a button on one side and a tall visual field on the other—intentionally off-center. Scroll-driven motion reveals content; the visual side can be a gradient mesh or image placeholder.

source_reference.when_to_use: On landing pages where you need both persuasion and atmosphere; works well mid-page before social proof or FAQs.
source_reference.do_not: Center both columns symmetrically or shrink the visual—this pattern needs asymmetry to feel designed.
source_reference.description: A two-column layout with copy and a button on one side and a tall visual field on the other—intentionally off-center. Scroll-driven motion reveals content; the visual side can be a gradient mesh or image placeholder.

name: Floating Card CTA
description: A rounded card that sits slightly rotated with layered shadow and a soft gradient fill—feels like a premium invite. Hover lifts and straightens the card subtly.

source_reference.when_to_use: When you want a “special offer” or limited beta feel; pairs well on light backgrounds as a focal island.
source_reference.do_not: Use this inside another heavy card container—let it breathe with margin and whitespace.
source_reference.description: A rounded card that sits slightly rotated with layered shadow and a soft gradient fill—feels like a premium invite. Hover lifts and straightens the card subtly.

name: Full-Bleed Image CTA
description: A full-bleed atmospheric image with a dark scrim, centered headline and supporting line, and a light button for maximum contrast. The background uses a subtle parallax-style offset on scroll.

source_reference.when_to_use: Brand storytelling moments, “mission” sections, or emotional closes before the footer.
source_reference.do_not: Use busy photography without enough overlay—text must stay effortlessly readable.
source_reference.description: A full-bleed atmospheric image with a dark scrim, centered headline and supporting line, and a light button for maximum contrast. The background uses a subtle parallax-style offset on scroll.

name: Smooth Accordion
description: Classic expandable FAQ with smooth height animation via Framer Motion `AnimatePresence`. Plus/minus icon rotates on toggle; clean borders between items. The most versatile pattern.

source_reference.when_to_use: Default FAQ blocks, help centers, product pages, and any list where users scan questions and expand one at a time (or multiple if you relax state).
source_reference.do_not: Use when you need instant visibility of all answers without interaction, or when the list is very long without search—pair with another pattern instead.
source_reference.description: Classic expandable FAQ with smooth height animation via Framer Motion `AnimatePresence`. Plus/minus icon rotates on toggle; clean borders between items. The most versatile pattern.

name: Two-Column Split
description: Questions in the left column; the right panel shows the selected answer. Selected question is highlighted. Desktop: side-by-side; mobile: stacks into an accordion-style flow. More interactive than a plain list.

source_reference.when_to_use: Marketing pages where you want a “focus” reading experience, fewer than ~12 questions, and emphasis on one answer at a time with strong visual hierarchy.
source_reference.do_not: Use for very long lists without search, or when users must compare multiple answers side-by-side in view at once.
source_reference.description: Questions in the left column; the right panel shows the selected answer. Selected question is highlighted. Desktop: side-by-side; mobile: stacks into an accordion-style flow. More interactive than a plain list.

name: Searchable FAQ
description: Search input at the top filters questions in real time. Non-matches fade out; matches stay prominent and matching text is highlighted. Ideal for larger FAQ sets.

source_reference.when_to_use: Ten or more items, documentation-style help, or when users arrive with a specific keyword in mind.
source_reference.do_not: Use for only two or three questions—the search affordance adds noise without benefit.
source_reference.description: Search input at the top filters questions in real time. Non-matches fade out; matches stay prominent and matching text is highlighted. Ideal for larger FAQ sets.

name: Categorized Tabs
description: FAQs grouped by category with a horizontal tab bar. Each category has its own accordion. Use when topics are clearly separate (e.g. General, Pricing, Technical).

source_reference.when_to_use: Mixed audiences, long FAQ sets split by intent, or when navigation by topic beats one long scroll.
source_reference.do_not: Use when categories are fuzzy or overlap heavily—users will not know which tab to open.
source_reference.description: FAQs grouped by category with a horizontal tab bar. Each category has its own accordion. Use when topics are clearly separate (e.g. General, Pricing, Technical).

name: Conversational FAQ
description: Questions styled as user bubbles on the right; answers as brand bubbles on the left. Staggered entrance; approachable, chat-like layout for friendly brands.

source_reference.when_to_use: Consumer brands, onboarding, support landing pages where tone should feel human and low-friction.
source_reference.do_not: Use for dense legal or compliance FAQs where neutral document styling is required.
source_reference.description: Questions styled as user bubbles on the right; answers as brand bubbles on the left. Staggered entrance; approachable, chat-like layout for friendly brands.

name: Tabbed Feature Showcase
description: Products or services with 3-5 distinct capabilities that each deserve their own visual. The tabs create exploration — users engage by clicking, not just scrolling. Pair with real product screenshots or custom illustrations.

source_reference.when_to_use: Products or services with 3-5 distinct capabilities that each deserve their own visual. The tabs create exploration — users engage by clicking, not just scrolling. Pair with real product screenshots or custom illustrations.
source_reference.do_not: Use generic placeholder images. Each tab should show something meaningfully different. If all tabs look the same, use a different pattern.

name: Horizontal Gallery Carousel
description: Portfolio showcases, case studies, project galleries. The horizontal scroll breaks the vertical rhythm of the page and creates a sense of exploration. Image-heavy content only — don't use for text-heavy features.

source_reference.when_to_use: Portfolio showcases, case studies, project galleries. The horizontal scroll breaks the vertical rhythm of the page and creates a sense of exploration. Image-heavy content only — don't use for text-heavy features.
source_reference.do_not: Use fewer than 4 items — the carousel loses its purpose. Each item needs a strong image.

name: Radial Orbital Timeline
description: Complex processes, product roadmaps, interconnected features. This is a showstopper — use it when you want the features section to be a memorable interactive experience. Works best with 5-8 nodes.

source_reference.when_to_use: Complex processes, product roadmaps, interconnected features. This is a showstopper — use it when you want the features section to be a memorable interactive experience. Works best with 5-8 nodes.
source_reference.do_not: Use for simple feature lists. The complexity is the point — if the content is simple, use a simpler pattern. Also avoid on mobile-first sites as the orbital layout needs screen real estate.

name: Stacked Reveal Cards
description: Storytelling-oriented features. Each feature gets its own full-width moment with a large image and descriptive text. The scroll-triggered reveal creates a cinematic feel. Works well when you have 3-5 features with strong imagery.

source_reference.when_to_use: Storytelling-oriented features. Each feature gets its own full-width moment with a large image and descriptive text. The scroll-triggered reveal creates a cinematic feel. Works well when you have 3-5 features with strong imagery.
source_reference.do_not: Use without compelling images. The large image areas demand quality visuals. Also avoid for more than 5 features — the vertical scroll becomes excessive.

name: Grid Columns Classic
description: Any business or SaaS site. The most versatile footer pattern — works with any brand, any color scheme. Let the content do the work.

source_reference.when_to_use: Any business or SaaS site. The most versatile footer pattern — works with any brand, any color scheme. Let the content do the work.
source_reference.do_not: Make all columns the same width with the same number of links. Vary the density — one column might have 6 links, another might have 3.

name: Animated Blur-In
description: Modern brands that want subtle polish. The blur-in animation on scroll makes the footer feel intentional rather than forgotten. The radial glow at top creates a natural visual boundary between content and footer.

source_reference.when_to_use: Modern brands that want subtle polish. The blur-in animation on scroll makes the footer feel intentional rather than forgotten. The radial glow at top creates a natural visual boundary between content and footer.
source_reference.do_not: Overdo the animation delays — keep them tight (0.1-0.4s range). Slow footers feel broken.

name: Minimal Mono
description: Tech, fintech, developer tools. The monospace font and bordered social buttons create a clean, functional aesthetic. Good when the footer should feel like a utility, not a design moment.

source_reference.when_to_use: Tech, fintech, developer tools. The monospace font and bordered social buttons create a clean, functional aesthetic. Good when the footer should feel like a utility, not a design moment.
source_reference.do_not: Add decorative elements — the whole point is restraint. No gradients, no icons inside the links, no hover animations beyond underline.

name: SVG Text Reveal
description: Creative agencies, portfolios, design studios. The SVG text hover effect is an interactive detail that rewards curiosity. The radial gradient background creates depth. Good as a conversation-starter footer.

source_reference.when_to_use: Creative agencies, portfolios, design studios. The SVG text hover effect is an interactive detail that rewards curiosity. The radial gradient background creates depth. Good as a conversation-starter footer.
source_reference.do_not: Use for content-heavy footers with many link columns — this pattern is more about a visual moment than navigation utility.

name: Brand Watermark
description: Brands with a strong name worth showcasing. The giant background text creates a bold visual anchor. The centered layout with floating logo badge is memorable. Good for brands that want their footer to feel like a closing statement.

source_reference.when_to_use: Brands with a strong name worth showcasing. The giant background text creates a bold visual anchor. The centered layout with floating logo badge is memorable. Good for brands that want their footer to feel like a closing statement.
source_reference.do_not: Use if the brand name is very long (5+ words) — the watermark text won't fit. Best with 1-2 word brand names.

name: Cybercore Grid
description: Dark, futuristic, tech-forward brands. AI, cybersecurity, gaming, blockchain. Creates an immersive first impression with zero images needed.

source_reference.when_to_use: Dark, futuristic, tech-forward brands. AI, cybersecurity, gaming, blockchain. Creates an immersive first impression with zero images needed.
source_reference.do_not: Use for warm/friendly brands, service businesses, or anything that needs to feel approachable. The aesthetic is deliberately cold and technical.

name: Centered Media Hero
description: Clean, modern brands. SaaS products, agencies, startups. The email capture makes it ideal for lead generation. The media block (image or video) showcases a product or creates atmosphere.

source_reference.when_to_use: Clean, modern brands. SaaS products, agencies, startups. The email capture makes it ideal for lead generation. The media block (image or video) showcases a product or creates atmosphere.
source_reference.do_not: Skip the media block — that's what makes this pattern different from a generic centered hero. The visual anchors the section.

name: Shader Atmosphere
description: Premium dark brands that want an immersive, moving background. Creative agencies, luxury tech, design tools. The mesh gradient creates a living, breathing atmosphere that no static image can match.

source_reference.when_to_use: Premium dark brands that want an immersive, moving background. Creative agencies, luxury tech, design tools. The mesh gradient creates a living, breathing atmosphere that no static image can match.
source_reference.do_not: Use on pages that need fast load times above all else — shaders add GPU load. Not for simple service businesses.

name: Mega Menu Dropdown
description: Websites with 5+ pages or nested sub-pages (services with sub-services, resources with blog/help/docs). The dropdown menus organize complex navigation without overwhelming the top bar.

source_reference.when_to_use: Websites with 5+ pages or nested sub-pages (services with sub-services, resources with blog/help/docs). The dropdown menus organize complex navigation without overwhelming the top bar.
source_reference.do_not: Use for simple 3-4 page sites — it's overkill. The dropdowns would have one item each, which feels empty.

name: Minimal Sticky
description: Clean, modern sites where the navigation should be invisible until needed. The backdrop blur appears only on scroll, keeping the hero section clean. Best for 3-5 page sites with simple navigation.

source_reference.when_to_use: Clean, modern sites where the navigation should be invisible until needed. The backdrop blur appears only on scroll, keeping the hero section clean. Best for 3-5 page sites with simple navigation.
source_reference.do_not: Use with complex dropdown menus — this pattern is about simplicity. If you need dropdowns, use pattern 1 or 4.

name: Shrinking Pill
description: Premium brands that want a subtle, delightful scroll interaction. The header starts full-width and shrinks into a floating pill on scroll — feels polished and intentional. Best for sites with a strong hero section.

source_reference.when_to_use: Premium brands that want a subtle, delightful scroll interaction. The header starts full-width and shrinks into a floating pill on scroll — feels polished and intentional. Best for sites with a strong hero section.
source_reference.do_not: Use if the site has many nav items — the pill shape can't hold more than 4-5 links comfortably.

name: Enterprise Two-Column
description: SaaS, B2B, enterprise products with multiple product areas and company pages. The two-column dropdown with icon-boxed items feels organized and professional. Good for 6+ nav items organized into categories.

source_reference.when_to_use: SaaS, B2B, enterprise products with multiple product areas and company pages. The two-column dropdown with icon-boxed items feels organized and professional. Good for 6+ nav items organized into categories.
source_reference.do_not: Use for simple sites — the two-column dropdowns will look sparse with few items.

name: Floating Capsule
description: Creative, portfolio, or minimal sites. The floating capsule feels lightweight and modern — it doesn't touch the edges of the viewport. Best with 3-4 nav items max. Creates a premium first impression.

source_reference.when_to_use: Creative, portfolio, or minimal sites. The floating capsule feels lightweight and modern — it doesn't touch the edges of the viewport. Best with 3-4 nav items max. Creates a premium first impression.
source_reference.do_not: Overcrowd with nav items — the capsule shape constrains width. If you need more than 4-5 items, use a different pattern.

name: Glassmorphism Cards
description: Premium brands, dark-theme sites, creative agencies. The frosted glass cards over a gradient background create depth. Best when you want pricing to feel like a premium experience, not a comparison table.

source_reference.when_to_use: Premium brands, dark-theme sites, creative agencies. The frosted glass cards over a gradient background create depth. Best when you want pricing to feel like a premium experience, not a comparison table.
source_reference.do_not: Use with a light, corporate aesthetic — the glassmorphism looks out of place. Needs a dark or vibrant background to work.

name: Animated Toggle with Border Trail
description: SaaS products with monthly/yearly pricing. The spring-animated toggle feels premium and the glowing border trail on the featured plan draws attention. Works with both light and dark themes.

source_reference.when_to_use: SaaS products with monthly/yearly pricing. The spring-animated toggle feels premium and the glowing border trail on the featured plan draws attention. Works with both light and dark themes.
source_reference.do_not: Skip the toggle animation — it's the key differentiator. A static toggle loses the premium feel. Also make sure yearly pricing actually saves money or the toggle is pointless.

name: Spring Counter Row
description: A horizontal row of three or four headline metrics. Each value animates from zero to its target with a spring-eased motion when the row enters the viewport. Typography stays light: oversized numerals, optional suffix (`+`, `%`, `M`), and a short label underneath.

source_reference.when_to_use: Landing hero follow-ups, product pages that need quick credibility without visual noise, or above-the-fold “by the numbers” bands where space is tight and motion should feel premium, not flashy.
source_reference.do_not: Use for more than four stats (readability breaks); stack heavy decoration or icons here—the row is intentionally minimal; or pair with another full-width animated stats block on the same fold.
source_reference.description: A horizontal row of three or four headline metrics. Each value animates from zero to its target with a spring-eased motion when the row enters the viewport. Typography stays light: oversized numerals, optional suffix (`+`, `%`, `M`), and a short label underneath.

name: Dark Band with Glow
description: A full-width dark strip that reads as a section divider. Stats sit in one row; each number has a soft outer glow tinted with the theme primary. Count-up runs once when the band scrolls into view—compact and high-contrast.

source_reference.when_to_use: Breaking long pages between narrative blocks, dark-themed sites, or when you want metrics to feel like a branded “ribbon” without a full card grid.
source_reference.do_not: Nest complex charts or long copy inside the band; use light text on light backgrounds without adjusting `theme` contrast; or duplicate this band back-to-back (visual fatigue).
source_reference.description: A full-width dark strip that reads as a section divider. Stats sit in one row; each number has a soft outer glow tinted with the theme primary. Count-up runs once when the band scrolls into view—compact and high-contrast.

name: Bordered Grid Cards
description: A responsive grid (four columns on large screens, two on medium, one on small) of bordered cards. Each card shows a Lucide icon, a large metric, and a short description. Hover adds a slight lift and shadow; alternating cards use a subtle background tint for rhythm.

source_reference.when_to_use: “Why us” or capability sections where each number needs context (icon + copy), dashboards marketing pages, or when stats should feel like tangible deliverables.
source_reference.do_not: Cram more than one primary number per card; use clashing icon colors per card—keep icon tint tied to `theme.colors.primary`; or omit labels (accessibility suffers).
source_reference.description: A responsive grid (four columns on large screens, two on medium, one on small) of bordered cards. Each card shows a Lucide icon, a large metric, and a short description. Hover adds a slight lift and shadow; alternating cards use a subtle background tint for rhythm.

name: Parallax Background Stats
description: A section with a soft gradient or pattern backdrop. Each stat uses two layers: an enormous, semi-transparent numeral for depth and a smaller, bold foreground value plus label. Optional slight parallax on the background layer via `motion` scroll offsets.

source_reference.when_to_use: Editorial homepages, brand-forward landing pages, or anywhere typography should carry the story while numbers still land as proof.
source_reference.do_not: Use low contrast between ghost and foreground numbers; add more than three stats (layout gets muddy); or rely on this as the only readable copy—keep labels crisp.
source_reference.description: A section with a soft gradient or pattern backdrop. Each stat uses two layers: an enormous, semi-transparent numeral for depth and a smaller, bold foreground value plus label. Optional slight parallax on the background layer via `motion` scroll offsets.

name: Inline Proof Strip
description: A single horizontal line of compact stats separated by vertical rules—social proof sized to sit between sections. No cards or panel backgrounds; numbers spring-animate once in view. Reads like a caption: “500+ clients · 12 years · 98% satisfaction · $50M+ revenue”.

source_reference.when_to_use: Between testimonials and pricing, under a logo row, or as a subtle trust strip where vertical space is minimal.
source_reference.do_not: Wrap lines with more than four fragments on mobile without stacking; use decorative icons (breaks the text-only brief); or set font sizes so large they compete with the hero.
source_reference.description: A single horizontal line of compact stats separated by vertical rules—social proof sized to sit between sections. No cards or panel backgrounds; numbers spring-animate once in view. Reads like a caption: “500+ clients · 12 years · 98% satisfaction · $50M+ revenue”.

name: Magazine Layout
description: An asymmetric CSS grid where the lead member occupies a wide hero card (two columns) with a large image and full biography. Supporting members sit in a denser sub-grid of smaller cards. Photos use a dark gradient overlay on hover to reveal role and a short line of bio copy—editorial, print-magazine energy.

source_reference.when_to_use: You want hierarchy (founder / lead first), storytelling, and a strong visual anchor. Best when you have at least one high-quality portrait and copy for a “featured” person.
source_reference.do_not: Use when every member must feel equal in weight, when you lack imagery (prefer initials placeholders only if unavoidable), or when the section must stay strictly uniform card sizes.
source_reference.description: An asymmetric CSS grid where the lead member occupies a wide hero card (two columns) with a large image and full biography. Supporting members sit in a denser sub-grid of smaller cards. Photos use a dark gradient overlay on hover to reveal role and a short line of bio copy—editorial, print-magazine energy.

name: Horizontal Scroll Strip
description: A single row of team members inside a horizontally scrollable container. Each item is photo-first: large circular or softly rounded-square portraits, name, then role beneath. The whole strip animates in when it enters the viewport (scroll-triggered). Copy stays minimal; imagery carries the section.

source_reference.when_to_use: Many headshots, a “cast” or roster feel, or layouts where vertical space is tight. Strong on mobile where horizontal swipe is natural.
source_reference.do_not: Use when SEO-heavy bios are required above the fold, or when keyboard-only users cannot discover scroll (ensure focusable region / visible hint if needed).
source_reference.description: A single row of team members inside a horizontally scrollable container. Each item is photo-first: large circular or softly rounded-square portraits, name, then role beneath. The whole strip animates in when it enters the viewport (scroll-triggered). Copy stays minimal; imagery carries the section.

name: Staggered Cards
description: A loose, organic layout: cards sit at alternating vertical offsets (`translate-y`) so the section feels hand-placed rather than rigid. Each card shows photo, name, role, and a one-line quote. On hover, a strip of social links fades in. Children stagger into view with `motion` as you scroll.

source_reference.when_to_use: Personality-forward brands, creative studios, or when you want quotes as social proof without a separate testimonial block.
source_reference.do_not: Use when strict alignment or dense data tables matter; staggered layouts need breathing room.
source_reference.description: A loose, organic layout: cards sit at alternating vertical offsets (`translate-y`) so the section feels hand-placed rather than rigid. Each card shows photo, name, role, and a one-line quote. On hover, a strip of social links fades in. Children stagger into view with `motion` as you scroll.

name: Minimal List
description: Zero photography. A vertical list of rows: **Name** in a monospace or serif face, **Role** in muted tone, and a single line of bio. Subtle dividers separate rows; hovering highlights the row background. Extremely editorial and text-first—like credits or a masthead page.

source_reference.when_to_use: No assets yet, typography-led brands, legal or studio pages where faces are optional, or fast-loading sections.
source_reference.do_not: Use when faces are essential for trust (e.g. some healthcare or coaching sites), or when the list is very long without grouping (consider pagination or anchors).
source_reference.description: Zero photography. A vertical list of rows: **Name** in a monospace or serif face, **Role** in muted tone, and a single line of bio. Subtle dividers separate rows; hovering highlights the row background. Extremely editorial and text-first—like credits or a masthead page.

name: Overlapping Avatars with Expand
description: A compact default: circular avatars overlap in a horizontal row (negative margin). Clicking or hovering a member expands that avatar into a full card showing name, role, and bio; siblings slide aside with `motion` layout semantics. Placeholder initials appear in colored circles when photos are missing.

source_reference.when_to_use: Dense headers, “meet the team” above the fold, or interactive micro-UX. Good when you want playfulness without a tall grid.
source_reference.do_not: Use as the only team content if accessibility requires predictable focus order without hover—pair with click-to-pin or ensure keyboard parity in production.
source_reference.description: A compact default: circular avatars overlap in a horizontal row (negative margin). Clicking or hovering a member expands that avatar into a full card showing name, role, and bio; siblings slide aside with `motion` layout semantics. Placeholder initials appear in colored circles when photos are missing.

name: Draggable Card Stack
description: Fun, approachable brands. The drag interaction invites exploration — users discover testimonials by swiping. Works well with 3-5 testimonials. Creates a memorable micro-interaction.

source_reference.when_to_use: Fun, approachable brands. The drag interaction invites exploration — users discover testimonials by swiping. Works well with 3-5 testimonials. Creates a memorable micro-interaction.
source_reference.do_not: Use for formal/corporate brands — the playful drag gesture feels casual. Also avoid with more than 5 testimonials as the stack becomes unwieldy.

name: Social Proof Tweet
description: Tech companies, SaaS, developer tools — anywhere social media credibility matters. The tweet format is instantly recognizable and feels authentic. The reply thread adds conversational depth. Use real tweets when possible.

source_reference.when_to_use: Tech companies, SaaS, developer tools — anywhere social media credibility matters. The tweet format is instantly recognizable and feels authentic. The reply thread adds conversational depth. Use real tweets when possible.
source_reference.do_not: Fabricate tweets from real people — that's deceptive. Use real customer quotes styled as social posts, or clearly fictional examples with fictional names.

name: Expandable Carousel
description: When each testimonial deserves space — long quotes, detailed stories, transformation narratives. The horizontal scroll creates exploration; the expand-on-click reveals the full story. Best with 4-8 testimonials that have real depth.

source_reference.when_to_use: When each testimonial deserves space — long quotes, detailed stories, transformation narratives. The horizontal scroll creates exploration; the expand-on-click reveals the full story. Best with 4-8 testimonials that have real depth.
source_reference.do_not: Use with short one-line quotes — the expand interaction feels empty if there's nothing more to reveal.

description: When you have MANY testimonials (10+) and want to show volume. The continuous vertical scroll creates an impression of overwhelming positive feedback. Works as a background element or as a dedicated testimonials section. Good for SaaS, marketplaces, platforms with many users.

name: Cinematic Image Gallery
description: High-end brands, luxury services, agencies where the people behind the testimonials matter as much as their words. The 3D image rotation with perspective creates a cinematic feel. The word-by-word blur-in animation makes the quote feel like it's being spoken. Best with 3-5 testimonials with photos.

source_reference.when_to_use: High-end brands, luxury services, agencies where the people behind the testimonials matter as much as their words. The 3D image rotation with perspective creates a cinematic feel. The word-by-word blur-in animation makes the quote feel like it's being spoken. Best with 3-5 testimonials with photos.
source_reference.do_not: Use without real photos — the entire impact comes from the image gallery. Placeholder avatars won't work. Also needs at least 3 testimonials for the rotation to feel natural.

name: Infinite Logo Marquee
description: Below the hero on any page. Shows client/partner logos in continuous motion. The edge blur creates a polished infinite-scroll effect. Best with 6-12 logos.

source_reference.when_to_use: Below the hero on any page. Shows client/partner logos in continuous motion. The edge blur creates a polished infinite-scroll effect. Best with 6-12 logos.
source_reference.do_not: Use with fewer than 5 logos — the repetition gap becomes visible.

name: Logo Grid with Accents
description: When you want logos to feel more substantial than a simple marquee. The bordered grid with plus-icon accents creates an editorial/architectural feel. Best with 4 or 8 logos to fill the grid evenly.

source_reference.when_to_use: When you want logos to feel more substantial than a simple marquee. The bordered grid with plus-icon accents creates an editorial/architectural feel. Best with 4 or 8 logos to fill the grid evenly.
source_reference.do_not: Use with an odd number of logos — the grid will look unbalanced. Also avoid if logos are very different sizes.

name: Integration Honeycomb
description: "Integrations" or "Works with" sections. The split layout puts a CTA next to a visual grid of integration icons. The octagonal clip-path on icons creates a unique, technical look. Best with 12-18 icons.

source_reference.when_to_use: "Integrations" or "Works with" sections. The split layout puts a CTA next to a visual grid of integration icons. The octagonal clip-path on icons creates a unique, technical look. Best with 12-18 icons.
source_reference.do_not: Use for client logos — this pattern is specifically for integration/tool icons. The hexagonal shape implies "connects with."

name: Masked Logo Slider
description: The simplest logo cloud. Just a smooth sliding row of logos with CSS mask fade on edges. No borders, no backgrounds — just logos floating. Best when you want social proof without visual weight.

source_reference.when_to_use: The simplest logo cloud. Just a smooth sliding row of logos with CSS mask fade on edges. No borders, no backgrounds — just logos floating. Best when you want social proof without visual weight.
source_reference.do_not: Make logos too large — they should be subtle, not dominant. Height of 16-20px is ideal.

name: Gradient Section Divider
description: Between any two sections that need a visual break. Provides three sub-patterns: a gradient mesh line, an animated pulse line, and a decorative rule with centered label. Mix and match based on the transition mood.

source_reference.when_to_use: Between any two sections that need a visual break. Provides three sub-patterns: a gradient mesh line, an animated pulse line, and a decorative rule with centered label. Mix and match based on the transition mood.
source_reference.do_not: Use between every section — that creates its own monotony. One or two per page is enough.
